title: Larry with a young soldier, Nui Ba Den
description: Larry stands among granite boulders with his arm around the shoulders of a smiling young soldier who holds a submachine gun. Larry's name tape — HUNNEWELL — is fully legible, with a U.S. ARMY tape on the opposite chest and a patch at his left pocket. Behind them, sandbags are stacked among boulders bearing painted inscriptions in red, and heavy cables run down the rock face to a dark metal cabinet.
researchNotes: Larry confirmed in conversation with his son (2026-08-17) that this is him. The survey had read the HUNNEWELL name tape; his own word, not the machine reading, is what anchors the identity, alongside his 2026-08-15 self-identifications in VN-0015 and VN-0022. Still open from this frame, and each is a question for him (so no hypothesis about any of them is kept in this record; see research/photos/held-from-records-2026-09-14.md): who the young soldier is, what the cabinet behind them held, whose weapon he is holding, and what the pocket patch said (a re-scan target). The painted rock inscriptions are unread. The setting matches VN-0009/VN-0006, and on 2026-09-12 Larry named the place himself — 'Location: Nui Ba Den' (giscus-vn-0028-c18416060.json) — so the location is now set on his word.
